themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK—a 3,100% increase from the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a sudden public health or environmental hazard emerging in CD 103.
evidence: 16 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 31.0, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Prior spike of 16 complaints 2 weeks ago suggests sustained problem, not isolated incident
Aligns with Gothamist coverage of 'wild west' private trash industry in Chinatown (2026-04-03), indicating sanitation infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Investigate whether private trash carters or recent sanitation service changes are leaving waste exposed, attracting rodents/wildlife
Interview DSNY, local businesses, and residents about what triggered the spike and whether it correlates with trash collection gaps

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK—a 1,500% spike from 0.2 weekly average—indicating sudden disruption or misuse in local parks, possibly tied to encampment growth or unregulated street activity.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.67)
Encampment complaints remain elevated at 546 over 90 days, suggesting concurrent homelessness/public space conflict
Community board repeatedly requests park reconstruction/upgrades, indicating long-standing maintenance and safety gaps
reporting_angles: Document what specific rule violations are occurring this week (illegal structures, noise, trespassing) and map against encampment locations
Interview Parks Dept on enforcement capacity and whether the spike reflects new behavior or reactive reporting

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Building/use violations jumped to 14 LAST WEEK—a 600% increase from 2.0 weekly average—coinciding with 726 DOB permits filed in 90 days (615 alterations), suggesting enforcement gaps or illegal conversions amid active development.
evidence: 14 building/use violation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 9.07, second-highest anomaly)
726 DOB permits filed in past 90 days (615 alterations) indicates dense construction activity; 5 active ULURP applications suggest ongoing zoning pressure
Spike may reflect illegal subdivisions, unpermitted conversions, or overcrowding tied to housing pressure in high-demand district
reporting_angles: Cross-reference building violation addresses with DOB active permits and ULURP applications to identify pattern of illegal work or non-compliance
Interview HPD/DOB on whether inspection capacity is keeping pace with alteration volume, or if developers are circumventing rules

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Street Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped 208% to 15 LAST WEEK (vs. 4.9 weekly average), and illegal posting spiked 2,300% to 3 LAST WEEK (vs. 0.1 weekly average), signaling degradation of street conditions tied to trash industry shifts and enforcement gaps.
evidence: Illegal dumping: 15 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.27)
Illegal posting: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
Gothamist published 'Reforms to wild west private trash industry in Manhattan's Chinatown' (2026-04-03), indicating industry restructuring is causing visible street impacts
reporting_angles: Trace the Gothamist trash industry story; identify which cart operators or waste processors are cited in dumping/posting complaints
Interview DSNY and community board about whether new trash carters lack proper bins, routes, or enforcement compliance

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK—a 500% increase from 0.5 weekly average—while bike rack complaints hit 4 LAST WEEK (967% above baseline), suggesting concentrated street furniture degradation or vandalism.
evidence: Street sign damage: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0)
Bike rack complaints: 4 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.21)
Community board budget requests repeatedly cite 'improve trash removal and cleanliness' and 'vacant lot cleaning,' indicating broader public realm neglect
reporting_angles: Map street furniture complaints geographically to identify whether damage is concentrated in specific blocks or commercial corridors
Interview DOT on maintenance backlog and whether staffing/budget cuts are delaying repairs
